newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 3.

text.p: It's stealthy revolution, says Moore: Separate laws for Maoris were constitutional revolution by stealth, Labour MP Mike Moore said on Monday. Page 1.

$25m given to groups researching Treaty claims: The Crown Forestry Rental Trust has given more than $25 million to groups researching Treaty of Waitangi Claims, according to figures issued today by Finance Minister Bill Birch. Page 2.

Anderton wants super accord to be revived: The superannuation accord should be revived after the September referendum on compulsory retirement saving and strengthened by having its own secretariat, Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Monday. Page 2.
Profitable TSB hunts for custom: TSB Bank is aiming to more than double its mortgage customers from outside the Taranaki region in the next 12 months. Page 17.
Pit problems cut Macraes forecast: Instability in two walls of Round Hill pit in East Otago has forced Macraes Mining to reduce its forecast gold production by about 5000 ounces this year. Page 17.
Retailers demand Eftpos answers: Shopping deadlock: Retailers are demanding answers about an Eftpos breakdown after millions of customer dollars were affected on Monday.
Rivals make Amcor work for NZ profits: Australian-based Amcor is feeling the pinch from increased competition in the paper and packaging business in New Zealand.

Grape vintage falls short: This year's grape vintage of 64,000 tonnes has delivered about 18 percent less than anticipated, and the country's biggest producer, Montana Wines, is, for the first time, offering to buy surplus wine from smaller producers.

New technology boosts chance of oil strike: Energy companies Shell and Todd are confident they can commercially extract oil from an area off the Taranaki coast which until now has been considered uneconomic.
School in drugs clamp: Ten students at Shirley Boys' High School have been suspended for using and supplying drugs.
